content_sections.heading: About NLSIU
content_sections.text: As per the notifications, the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) was established in 1987 to be a pioneer in legal education. Over the last three decades, the University has evolved as an innovative leader in law, social sciences, humanities, and public policy education and research in India. It has also been ranked first among the law universities in the National Institute Ranking Framework (NIRF) for the last eight years. The University invites applications from exceptionally well-qualified individuals dedicated to academic teaching, scholarship, and institutional service.

content_sections.heading: NLSIU Assistant Professor Recruitment 2026 Notification-wise Details
content_sections.text: The HAL Defence Public Sector Chair was established in 2012 through an endowment corpus from Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. The key objective of the Chair is to expand teaching and research on relevant areas of business laws, which include contracts management, defence sector procurement, dispute settlement, and environmental compliance among other areas. The Chair further seeks to strengthen academic learning and pedagogy, contribute to policy dialogue and reform, foster a community of world class researchers and academics, facilitate training programmes, hold national and regional convenings, and produce high-impact legal research. The Chair will be part of a dedicated team of faculty members working to advance learning and scholarship in the areas of contract law, property law, and other areas of business law intersecting with the defence sector. The responsibilities include: Teaching Deliver undergraduate and postgraduate courses; Supervise student assignments, submissions, and thesis (as required); Evaluate students through examinations, presentations, and assignments as required. Research Contribute to designing and expanding the research agenda of the Chair; Publish in academic journals, books, and media platforms; Develop research proposals and grant applications; Organise guest lectures, public talks, and panel discussions on subject areas of the Chair as required; Develop training programmes in the areas of contracts, dispute resolution, negotiations etc. with special reference to defence sector; Conceptualize and organize an annual conference on defence sector laws; Participate in stakeholder meetings and contribute to policy and reform dialogues as required. Administrative Serve on university committees and provide other institutional services as required. The notification adds that serving under the Chair provides an excellent opportunity for emerging scholars to advance their research, demonstrate thought leadership in their field, and make meaningful contributions to evidence-based policy discussions and reform initiatives. As per the notification, NLSIU along with the Department of Revenue, Government of India, has established the Department of Revenue (DOR) to recognize scholars and teachers in the field of taxation law, anti-corruption, and foreign exchange regulation. The stated aim is to produce high quality research, strengthen pedagogy, engage in public policy dialogue and attract world class researchers and academicians to the University. The DOR Chair Assistant Professor is expected to perform the following functions: Contribute to teaching, research, and scholarship in taxation laws at the University; Conduct training and capacity building programmes including for DOR officials as required; Provide legal opinion and analysis on related laws to DOR officials as required; Render active support in all related topics as mutually agreed to with the primary objective of enhancing the knowledge and professional skills of DoR exe

content_sections.heading: NLSIU Assistant Professor Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Eligibility is defined through Appendix A of each notification, titled “Minimum Qualifications for Recruitment to Regular Posts of Teachers in the University (per UGC Regulations, 2018)”. All six notifications require the Essential Qualifications in Section I. The two permanent-post notifications (Nos. 20/2026 and 21/2026) additionally refer to Section II.1. The notifications also state that the prescribed essential qualifications/experience are the bare minimum, and that merely possessing them will not entitle a candidate to be called for an interview. The qualification should have been obtained from recognized Universities/Institutions.

content_sections.heading: NLSIU Assistant Professor Qualification
content_sections.text: A Master’s Degree with at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade in a point-scale, wherever the grading system is followed). A relaxation of 5% may be provided at the graduate and master’s level for the Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Differently abled categories for the purpose of eligibility and for assessing good academic record during direct recruitment to teaching positions. A relaxation of 5% may be provided to the Ph.D Degree holders who obtained their Master’s Degree prior to 19 September 1991. The eligibility marks of 55% marks or an equivalent grade in a point scale prescribed by these regulations and the relaxation of 5% to the categories mentioned above are permissible, based on only the qualifying marks without including any grace mark procedures. Section II.1 is titled “Assistant Professor (Law)” in Notification No. 20/2026 and “Assistant Professor (Humanities & Social Sciences)” in Notification No. 21/2026. The conditions are the same in both and are given below as per the notifications. Option A: The candidate must have cleared the National Eligibility Test (NET) conducted by the UGC or the CSIR, or a similar test accredited by the UGC, like SLET/SET, subject to the following exemptions: OR Option B: The Ph.D degree has been obtained from a foreign university/institution with a ranking among the top 500 in the World University Ranking (at any time) by any one of the following: (i) Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), (ii) the Times Higher Education (THE) or (iii) the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) of the Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Shanghai). Notification Nos. 22/2026, 23/2026, 24/2026 and 25/2026 refer only to Section I of Appendix A. Section II.1 (NET/Ph.D. conditions) is not referenced in these four notifications. Section II.1 does not form part of the Appendix A attached to them.
